guidance.source: skill-creator SKILL.md, installed at /mnt/skills/examples/skill-creator/SKILL.md (read from disk, verbatim)
guidance.quote:
Skills use a three-level loading system:
1. **Metadata** (name + description) - Always in context (~100 words)
2. **SKILL.md body** - In context whenever skill triggers (<500 lines ideal)
3. **Bundled resources** - As needed (unlimited, scripts can execute without loading)
Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines; if you're approaching this limit, add an additional layer of hierarchy along with clear pointers about where the model using the skill should go next to follow up.

**description**: When to trigger, what it does. This is the primary triggering mechanism - include both what the skill does AND specific contexts for when to use it. All "when to use" info goes here, not in the body.

**Domain organization**: When a skill supports multiple domains/frameworks, organize by variant:
```
cloud-deploy/
├── SKILL.md (workflow + selection)
└── references/
    ├── aws.md
    ├── gcp.md
    └── azure.md
```
Claude reads only the relevant reference file.
Skills appear in Claude's `available_skills` list with their name + description, and Claude decides whether to consult a skill based on that description.

The description field in SKILL.md frontmatter is the primary mechanism that determines whether Claude invokes a skill. After creating or improving a skill, offer to optimize the description for better triggering accuracy.

problem_statement: The 102 skills are individually well-formed against the Agent Skills guidance - no description breaches the 1,024-character cap, only one body exceeds 500 lines, and 714 KB of detail is correctly parked in one-level references - but the structure discloses badly in the aggregate: about 20,000 tokens of description are resident before any work starts, 30 of those descriptions open with the same four words, 44 skills are unreachable from the 514-edge graph, and the loading rule the repo states produces 24 to 44 skills per door against T9.5's budget of 11.

options.name: A. Keep 102; make the door path the loading rule instead of a curated table

load_path_per_door.basis: curated list becomes normative; transitive closure stops being the instruction

changes_required: README.md: replace 'pulls in that skill plus what it names under builds_on' and 'load the -implement sibling when writing code' with 'load the door path; builds_on is provenance, not a reading list'
docs/architecture/load-path.md: regenerate with both numbers (curated and transitive) so the budget claim is honest
tools/validate_skills.py: add a check that each door path is <= 11 and that every name on it exists
no change to schemas/skill.schema.json, docs/skill-manifest.json, kb ids, or any ceremony record
options.risk: Cheapest and least disruptive, but it fixes the number by redefining the rule. The ~20,000-token metadata floor and the 44 zero-fan-in leaves are untouched, and a reader who follows builds_on - which is what the graph, the manifest symmetry check and skill-graph.md all present as the structure - still lands on 24 to 44 skills. T9.5 would be met on paper and not in the hand.

options.name: B. Fold each -implement facet into references/implementation.md of its ideal, exactly as the -use facet was folded on 2026-09-03

load_path_per_door.note: the +implement inflation to 40-44 disappears; the ideal-only closure of 24-26 does not

changes_required: tools/manifest_facets.py: the whole facet expansion (expand, sections, check) and its documented facet rules retire; 5 -implement references in the file

tools/validate_skills.py: 8 -implement/-use suffix sites, including the rule that only a non-implement cap- skill must carry adapters - the adapters table moves onto the ideal, whose body is already the heavier facet (median 4,148 words)
tools/skill_graph.py (4 sites, folding already partly implemented), tools/render_guide.py (5), tools/acceptance_check.py (3)
schemas/skill.schema.json: name pattern and the per-facet expectations
docs/skill-manifest.json: remove 44 entries and repair used_by symmetry on the survivors
every ceremony record under kb/ceremonies/ that names an -implement skill by id (71 records present) and every harness provenance.json that does the same
options.risk: Highest machinery cost, and the measurement argues against the usual reason for doing it: duplication between the facets is only about 12 percent of implement rows, so this merges content that is genuinely distinct. It also destroys 44 trigger surfaces - descriptions like 'Load it when writing or reviewing the code that produces a failure' - and there is no trigger eval in this repo to show the surviving 58 descriptions still fire on those prompts. The ideal bodies risk breaching the token ceiling that finding S64-004 already flags.

options.name: C. Route, do not merge: one door-index skill, and a description budget

load_path_per_door.basis: door-index + the curated path, named by the index rather than derived by closure; every door stays at or under 11 by construction and the index is the one skill a cold caller has to find

changes_required: one new skill (proposed name seam-doors or cap-entry-index) whose only job is to name the <= 11 skills for each of the four doors and their -implement siblings; its body is a table, so it is small, and docs/architecture/load-path.md becomes its rendered reference

its description is written for the question a caller actually asks - 'which skills do I load to run one document through the human / event / schedule / external door' - which is the one question no current description answers (S64-005)

schemas/skill.schema.json: lower description maxLength from 1024 to about 600 and add the trigger-clause requirement; then trim the 102 descriptions, which drops always-resident metadata from ~20,259 tokens to roughly 12,000

rewrite the 30 'How to build the' and 15 'The ideal state of' openings so the first clause discriminates rather than labels the facet, and make each ideal name its -implement sibling (currently 0 of 58 do) so the 44 zero-fan-in leaves become reachable from inside the skill system
tools/validate_skills.py: description length and stem-collision checks
README.md counts corrected (S64-007); no change to docs/skill-manifest.json entries, kb ids, ceremony records, or harness provenance
options.risk: Shortening descriptions touches the exact field the guidance calls the primary triggering mechanism, and this repo has no trigger eval, so the trim must be measured rather than asserted. skill-creator ships that harness (scripts/run_loop.py plus a 20-query should-trigger / should-not-trigger set), so the mitigation is available; skipping it would be the failure mode. Adds a 103rd skill, which is the wrong direction if judged on count alone.

recommendation: Take Option C. It is the only option that moves the two numbers the guidance and T9.5 actually bind - always-resident metadata from about 20,259 tokens to about 12,000, and load path per door from a mechanical 24-44 down to 8-10 named by an index rather than derived by closure - without touching the manifest, the kb ids, the ceremony records or the harness provenance. It also answers S64-005 directly: the four-door question is the one a caller asks first and the one no description currently answers, and giving it a skill is cheaper and more discoverable than continuing to answer it in README.md. Do not take Option B now. The measurement says the ideal/implement split is not a duplication problem - only about 12 percent of implement rows name or restate the ideal, and identical rendered sentences are render boilerplate - so folding 44 skills would merge distinct content and destroy 44 working trigger surfaces to fix a discovery problem that a description rewrite fixes for a fraction of the machinery. Revisit B only after a trigger eval exists, using skill-creator's run_loop harness, and only if it shows the ideal descriptions already win the prompts the implement descriptions win today. Do not take Option A alone: redefining the rule so the curated table becomes normative satisfies T9.5 on paper while leaving a reader who follows builds_on - which the graph, the manifest symmetry check and skill-graph.md all present as the structure - on 24 to 44 skills. Option A's README and load-path.md corrections should be folded into C as its first step.

answers_to_the_owner_questions.is_the_layering_earning_its_keep: Partly. The seven layers earn their keep as a namespace and as validator machinery - the prefix drives the LAYERS check, the per-layer table budgets and the graph's focal groups - but they are not a disclosure mechanism: only 113 of 514 builds_on edges stay inside a layer, so a layer is never what a reader loads. What actually organises reading is the door, and the door is not a layer. Keep the layers; stop expecting them to bound the load path.
answers_to_the_owner_questions.is_ideal_implement_the_right_cut: Yes as a cut, no as a packaging. Measured duplication is about 12 percent of implement rows and the identical sentences are boilerplate, so the content genuinely differs and does not belong in references/ of one skill on redundancy grounds. But 44 skills with zero graph fan-in, 3 of 58 sibling cross-references and 30 identical description openings is the wrong way to ship a real distinction. Fix the reachability and the descriptions before considering the fold.
answers_to_the_owner_questions.are_descriptions_doing_the_triggering_jo: They are doing half of it. 88 of 102 carry an explicit 'Load it when' clause, which is what the guidance asks a description for, and none breaches the 1,024-character cap. But at a mean of 136.9 words they are above skill-creator's ~100-word metadata budget, they total roughly 20,259 always-resident tokens, and 45 of them open with one of two identical stems - so on the facet where discrimination matters most they signal what kind of skill this is rather than when to pick this one.
answers_to_the_owner_questions.is_102_the_right_count: 102 is not the problem; the metadata weight and the unreachable leaves are. The guidance explicitly contemplates 100+ skills and asks the description to carry the selection. At 102 skills and 794 characters each the descriptions are the binding constraint, not the count. Cutting to 58 would buy about 8,000 tokens and cost 44 trigger surfaces; trimming descriptions buys the same 8,000 tokens and costs none.
answers_to_the_owner_questions.what_a_cold_reader_finds_confusing: Four things, in order. First, which of the 102 to load for a door-shaped task: the answer exists at cap-consumption/references/load-path.md and nothing advertises it. Second, whether -implement is a second skill or a section of the first: nothing in the graph links them and only 3 descriptions say. Third, whether builds_on is a reading list or provenance: README says reading list, and following it costs 24 to 44 skills. Fourth, the counts - README says 100 skills and 11 build disciplines where disk says 102 and 12.

fine_as_is: Description length against the spec: 0 of 102 exceed the 1,024-character cap, max 1,011, and schemas/skill.schema.json already enforces minLength 40 / maxLength 1024. No breach exists here.

The trigger clause convention: 88 of 102 descriptions state both what the skill does and an explicit 'Load it when ...' list of contexts, which is exactly what the spec and skill-creator ask a description to carry.

references/ usage: 73 of 102 skills carry one, 96 files and 714 KB of schemas, adapter tables and worked calls kept out of context, every one of the 73 linked from its SKILL.md, and nesting is one level deep with no nested reference directories - this matches the progressive-disclosure pattern and the 'keep file references one level deep' guidance without exception.
SKILL.md line budget: median 229 lines, p90 328, and exactly one skill (seam-dispatch at 549) over the 500-line guideline. This does not need a programme.

The ideal/implement content cut itself: about 12 percent of implement rows name or restate the ideal and identical sentences are render boilerplate, so the two facets are not repeating each other. Leave the content alone.

The layer prefix as a namespace and as validator input: the LAYERS map, the prefix check, the per-layer table budgets and the graph's focal grouping all work off it and all pay for themselves. No reason to change the prefixes.

The precedent for retiring a facet is already proven: the -use facet was folded into its ideal with references/usage.md on 2026-09-03 (29 skills carry usage.md today), so if Option B is ever taken the repo already knows the move.

docs/skill-graph.md's own edge-budget discipline - splitting into focal groups against a stated 500-edge mermaid budget and citing X-skill-graph-001/002 - is exactly the kind of measured constraint this review is asking for elsewhere.
